item.title: 2017: Astros Beat Dodgers 5-1 in Game 7, Win First World Series
item.description: The Houston Astros defeated the Los Angeles Dodgers in Game 7 of the World Series at Dodger Stadium, 5–1, to claim their first World Series championship in 56 years of franchise history. Astros outfielder George Springer received World Series MVP honors. Photo: Keith Allison from Hanover, MD, USA (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 2025: Dodgers Beat Blue Jays in Game 7, Win Consecutive Titles
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers defeat the Toronto Blue Jays in game 7 for their ninth World Series championship, becoming the first MLB franchise with consecutive World Series titles since the 2000 New York Yankees. Photo: Redspork02 (CC BY-SA 4.0).

item.title: 2023: Rangers Beat Diamondbacks in Game 5, Win World Series
item.description: Texas Rangers defeat the Arizona Diamondbacks in Game 5 of the 2023 MLB World Series, to win the championship. Photo: The White House (Public domain).

item.title: 2021: Rangers Hire Ecker as Bench Coach and Offensive Coordinator
item.description: The Texas Rangers hired Ecker as their bench coach and offensive coordinator on November 1, 2021.

item.title: 2019: Mets Name Carlos Beltrán Manager on Three-Year Deal
item.description: The New York Mets named Carlos Beltrán their next manager for the following season. Beltrán reportedly earn approximately $3MM over the guaranteed three-year term, with a club option to follow. Photo: Keith Allison on Flickr (Original version) UCinternational (Crop) (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 2015: Royals Beat Mets 7-2 in 12 Innings, Win World Series
item.description: The Kansas City Royals captured the second World Series title in franchise history, with a 12-inning, 7–2 victory over the New York Mets in Game 5 at Citi Field. Once again, Kansas City came from behind to overcome a dominant start by Matt Harvey, who carried a 2–0 shutout through eight innings, then convinced Mets manager Terry Collins to let him remain in the game. Photo: slgckgc on Flickr (Original version) UCinternational (Crop) (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 2014: Anderson Marries Jessica Marie
item.description: Anderson and his wife Jessica Marie married on November 1, 2014 and divorced in 2023.

item.title: 2011: Parra Wins 2011 NL Gold Glove Award in Left Field
item.description: After an outstanding season defensively Parra was awarded the 2011 National League Left Fielder Gold Glove award on November 1, 2011. Photo: Mwinog2777 (CC BY-SA 3.0).

item.title: 2010: Giants Beat Rangers 3-1, Win First Title Since 1954
item.description: The San Francisco Giants defeat the Texas Rangers 3–1 to win the World Series four games to one. It is the franchise's first championship since 1954, and first since moving to San Francisco prior to the 1958 season. Photo: Ed Bierman on Flickr (Original version) UCinternational (Crop) (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 2010: Giants Beat Rangers in Five Games, End Curse of Coogan's Bluff
item.description: The postseason began on October 6, 2010, and ended on November 1, 2010, with the Giants defeating the Rangers in five games in the 2010 World Series, ending the Curse of Coogan's Bluff. Photo: Ed Bierman on Flickr (Original version) UCinternational (Crop) (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 2009: Yankees Rally in Ninth to Beat Phillies 7-4, Lead Series
item.description: The New York Yankees put themselves one win away from their 27th World Series title, after a three-run rally in the ninth inning, to beat the Philadelphia Phillies 7–4. Johnny Damon sparks the rally with a two-out single and two stolen bases off reliever and loser Brad Lidge, before a hit-by-pitch to Mark Teixeira and a go-ahead RBI double by Alex Rodriguez. A two-run, RBI-single by Jorge Posada seals the victory. Photo: edogisgod (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 2007: Dragons Sweep Nippon Ham Fighters, Win 2007 Japan Series
item.description: The Chunichi Dragons win the 2007 Japan Series over the Hokkaido Nippon Ham Fighters 4–1, losing the first game and sweeping the next four. The Dragons' Norihiro Nakamura is the series MVP. This was a rematch of the 2006 series, won by the Fighters in the same fashion. Game five was a combined perfect game, with starter Daisuke Yamai throwing eight innings, and Hitoki Iwase closing out the ninth. Photo: hfordsa on Flickr (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 2001: Jeter's Walk-off Homer Wins Game 4 After Martinez Tie
item.description: The New York Yankees pull off two incredible comebacks. With the Arizona Diamondbacks leading 3–1 with 2 outs in the 9th inning of Game 4 of the 2001 World Series, Tino Martinez hits a game-tying 2-run home run. One inning later (at 12:04 ET) Derek Jeter hits a walk-off home run to win Game 4, while fans wave a banner which says "Mr. November". Photo: Keith Allison (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 2001: H. Gabriel Murphy, 98, 40 Percent Owner of Washington Senators
item.description: H. Gabriel Murphy, 98, 40 percent owner of the Washington Senators/Minnesota Twins franchise from 1950 to 1984 who battled majority owner Calvin Griffith in court in an unsuccessful attempt to keep the team from abandoning the U.S. capital after the 1960 season.

item.title: 1978: Ron Guidry Wins AL Cy Young by Unanimous Vote
item.description: Ron Guidry of the New York Yankees is named winner of the American League Cy Young Award by a unanimous vote, taking all 28 first-place tallies.

item.title: 1976: 23 Players Granted Free Agency, Seven From Athletics
item.description: In the first off-season after the Seitz decision, 23 major-league players are granted free agency after they've played out their option years with their current clubs. Seven are members of the Oakland Athletics, including Sal Bando, Don Baylor, Bert Campaneris, future Hall-of-Famer Rollie Fingers, Joe Rudi and Gene Tenace. Photo: J.D. McCarthy (Public domain).

item.title: 1972: Mets Acquire Millán and Stone From Braves
item.description: Millán was acquired along with George Stone by the New York Mets from the Braves for Gary Gentry and Danny Frisella on November 1, 1972.

item.title: 1968: Denny McLain Unanimously Wins AL Cy Young
item.description: Denny McLain, the last MLB pitcher to win 30 games in a season, is the unanimous American League winner of the Cy Young Award. Four days from now, McLain will also be unanimously anointed the year's Al Most Valuable Player, winning all 20 first-place mentions and 280 total points.

item.title: 1967: Mike McCormick, 29, Wins 1967 NL Cy Young Award
item.description: Mike McCormick, former bonus baby and 1960 National League earned run average leader, is elected winner of the 1967 NL Cy Young Award. McCormick, 29, compiled a 22–10 (2.85) record with 14 complete games and five shutouts, in the first season of his second term with the San Francisco Giants.

item.title: 1957: Charlie Caldwell, 56, 1925 Yankees Pitcher, Coach
item.description: Charlie Caldwell, 56, pitcher for the 1925 New York Yankees, who later coached three sports at Williams College between 1925 and 1946, receiving AFCA Coach of the Year Award honors in 1950 and an induction to the College Football Hall of Fame in 1961. Photo: Photo copyrighted by Henry Parker, New York City. (Public domain).

item.title: 1951: Roy Campanella, 29, Named National League MVP
item.description: Brooklyn Dodgers catcher Roy Campanella is named National League Most Valuable Player, the first of three MVP awards he will receive during his Hall of Fame career. In 1951, Campanella, 29, batted .325, fourth in the NL, with 33 home runs and 108 run batted in in 143 games. Photo: ベースボール・マガジン社（Baseball Magazine Co. Ltd) (Public domain).

item.title: 1946: Athletics Select Ferris Fain, 25, in Rule 5 Draft
item.description: Among the selections in the Rule 5 draft is first baseman Ferris Fain, 25, a future two-time batting champion, acquired by the Philadelphia Athletics from the San Francisco Seals of the Pacific Coast League.

item.title: 1944: Branch Rickey Group Buys Quarter of Dodgers
item.description: A three-person group headlined by club president/general manager Branch Rickey acquires one-quarter ownership in the Dodgers from the Brooklyn Trust Company for an estimated $250,000. The stock, formerly held by the late Edward J. McKeever, has been managed by the bank on behalf of the McKeever estate. Photo: Rentschler (Public domain).

item.title: 1938: Ernie Lombardi, Reds Batting Champ, Named NL MVP
item.description: National League batting champ Ernie Lombardi of the Cincinnati Reds is named the Most Valuable Player. Chicago Cubs pitcher Bill Lee is the runner-up. Photo: Booklover117 (CC BY-SA 4.0).

item.title: 1922: Ira Thomas Buys Shreveport Gassers for $75,000
item.description: Former Philadelphia Athletics catcher Ira Thomas buys the Shreveport Gassers Texas League club for $75,000. Other former players who own pieces of minor league clubs include Ty Cobb (Augusta Georgians), Eddie Collins (Baltimore Orioles), and George Stallings (Rochester Red Wings). Photo: Paul Thompson (Public domain).

item.title: 1910: Bob Pettit, 49, Former Infielder, Outfielder
item.description: Bob Pettit, 49, infielder/outfielder from 1887 to 1891 for the NL Chicago White Stockings and AA Milwaukee Brewers. Photo: Unknown (Public domain).

item.title: 1892: Cy Young Posts 36–11 Record in 154-Game Season
item.description: Statistics for the first 154-game season show that Dan Brouthers of the Brooklyn Grooms was the top hitter with a .335 batting average, and Cy Young of the Cleveland Spiders the best pitcher with a 36–11 record and a .766 winning percentage. Photo: Goodwin & Company (Public domain).

item.title: 1882: Philadelphia Ball Club Limited Organizes Phillies
item.description: The history of the Philadelphia Phillies of Major League Baseball's National League began on November 1, 1882, with the organization of the Philadelphia Ball Club Limited. Photo: Philadelphia Ball Club Limited (Public domain).

item.title: 1878: Red Caps and Grays Play Odd Exhibition, Foul Bounds
item.description: The Boston Red Caps and the Providence Grays play an exhibition game with no outs on foul bounds and 6 balls for a walk to be given. Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).
